SANTA HAD A FLOATPLANE. ✈️🎁

Before this holiday tradition used helicopters, it started with a pilot saying thank you.

On Christmas Day in 1929, Capt. William Wincapaw dropped packages of coffee, candy, newspapers and other supplies to lighthouse families around Rockland, Maine. Their beacons had helped him navigate coastal flying—and he wanted to return the kindness.

Those flights grew into Flying Santa, a tradition that continues today through Friends of Flying Santa, bringing helicopter visits to Coast Guard families from Maine to New York.

Now the Aviation Museum of New Hampshire is sharing that history. Maritime historian Jeremy D’Entremont will present the story on November 19 at 7 p.m. at the museum in Londonderry. Admission is $10; museum members attend free.

A little airplane, a thoughtful delivery and a gesture that outlived its first flight. That’s aviation history worth smiling about. 💛

Source: Aviation Museum of New Hampshire, November 2, 2026; highlighted by General Aviation News on November 7.
